scope: Source review and CPU socketpair fixtures only; no model/owner/HTTP/service/kernel operations.
checks: Pending queue and total offered-byte caps are explicit; offer invokes at most four nonblocking send calls.
Partial writes retain exact order without replay; zero/invalid progress and socket errors abandon output only.
MSG_DONTWAIT keeps each kernel send nonblocking after sequential blocking-mode changes.
Positive Python socket timeouts are refused before send, preventing Python readiness waits despite MSG_DONTWAIT.
Final drain uses monotonic timeout restricted to0..1 seconds; repeated completion cannot resend accepted bytes.
SSE JSON encoding escapes CR/LF event delimiters and preserves UTF8 text.
Borrowed socket stays caller-owned and open; no peer-receipt or native lifecycle success is asserted.
resolved_findings: Per-send MSG_DONTWAIT added after initial mode-change boundedness review.
Filled-socket positive Python timeout reproduction blocked approximately0.0503s before guard; final regression now refuses a1s socket timeout promptly.
limitations: Caller must exclusively lend the socket; another thread must not mutate its Python timeout during the loan.
Caller must invoke final drain only after native SAVE/RELEASE disposition; this module does not enforce native order or semantic success.
Successful local send does not prove peer receipt; slow or disconnected readers abandon delivery only.
No integrated SSE endpoint, request-front streaming or real model execution is qualified by these CPU fixtures.
